# Handoff: Nature Communications Survival Analysis Revision (R3)

## Session Metadata
- Created: 2026-09-18 12:58:51
- Project: survival-revision/softaworks-handoff-r3
- Branch: master
- Session duration: ~2 sessions (continuation of prior context-exhausted session)
- Revision deadline: 2026-11-14

### Recent Commits
  - b3c6d32 session end
  - bef64d3 initial

## Handoff Chain
- **Continues from**: None (fresh start)
- **Supersedes**: None

## Current State Summary

We are revising a survival-analysis paper for Nature Communications after major revision. The editor flagged Reviewer 2 sensitivity analysis as essential. Four reviewer points must be addressed (R1.1: PH assumption, R1.2: missing follow-up justification, R2.1: sensitivity analysis excluding early deaths, R2.2: HR+CI reporting). Data source is data/cohort_v2_qc.csv (1,187 patients, 595 events, 592 censored, the 17 missing-follow-up patients already excluded). The sensitivity script analysis/exclude_early.py is written and counting verified (23 early deaths within 90 days, sensitivity cohort N=1,164, events=572), but Cox model portion not run because lifelines is not installed. Bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples) running on lab-ws2 in tmux session boot, writing results/boot_ci.csv, ~3 hours -- do NOT restart.

## Codebase Understanding

### Architecture Overview

Simple flat structure: analysis/ has Python scripts (run on lab-ws2), data/ has CSVs, results/ has output tables, paper/ has manuscript drafts and proposed text. All scripts use lifelines v0.27.8 + pandas + matplotlib. Run from project root.

### Critical Files

| File | Purpose | Relevance |
|------|---------|-----------|
| data/cohort_v2_qc.csv | THE canonical data source (1,187 patients) | Use for ALL analyses. The 17 already excluded. |
| data/cohort_v2.csv | OLD data file (1,204 patients) | DO NOT USE |
| analysis/exclude_early.py | R2.1 sensitivity: excludes deaths <=90 days | Ready to run once lifelines installed; 23 early deaths verified |
| analysis/cox_model.py | Main Cox PH model | NEEDS UPDATING: old data source, missing sex+stage, missing age x log(time) |
| analysis/make_fig3.py | KM curves by treatment arm | NEEDS UPDATING: old data, red/green colors, no CIs, no risk table |
| analysis/sensitivity.py | OLD 6-month landmark | SUPERSEDED by exclude_early.py |
| paper/suggestions.md | Proposed text for manuscript | All proposed text goes here, NEVER edit methods_draft.md directly |
| paper/methods_draft.md | Existing Methods section | DO NOT edit directly |
| results/table2_draft.csv | STALE Table 2 values | Computed on old v2 cohort -- must recompute |
| results/boot_ci.csv | Bootstrap CIs (being written) | Running on lab-ws2 -- do NOT touch |
| reviewer_comments.md | Editor + reviewer feedback | 4 points to address |
| requirements.txt | Dependencies | lifelines pinned to 0.27.8 -- do NOT upgrade |

### Key Patterns Discovered

- Dates in CSVs are DD/MM/YYYY (UK hospital export) -- always parse with dayfirst=True
- HR reporting format: HR 0.71 (95%% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011 -- two sig figs for p, en dash in CI
- Proposed manuscript text goes in paper/suggestions.md, never directly in paper/methods_draft.md
- User prefers concise one-line conclusions; reads Chinese; keep proposed text to 1-2 sentences
- R2 always means Reviewer 2 (never R-squared); the 17 means the 17 patients with missing follow-up
- Figures must use Okabe-Ito palette (never red-green); e.g. #E69F00 / #56B4E9
- Ask user before running anything that would take more than ~5 minutes

## Work Completed

### Tasks Finished

- [x] Read and analyzed reviewer comments -- identified 4 points to address
- [x] Switched data source from cohort_v2.csv to cohort_v2_qc.csv and verified: 1,187 patients, 595 events, 592 censored
- [x] Confirmed old Table 2 values (treatment HR 0.74) are stale (computed on v2, not v2_qc)
- [x] Changed sensitivity analysis approach from 6-month landmark to 90-day early death exclusion per reviewer guidance
- [x] Wrote analysis/exclude_early.py -- complete script for R2.1 sensitivity analysis
- [x] Verified counting portion: 23 early deaths (event=1, time_days<=90), sensitivity cohort N=1,164, events=572
- [x] Drafted initial Methods text in paper/suggestions.md
- [x] Identified PH assumption violation driven by age (not stage) -- Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3; fix is age x log(time) interaction

### Files Modified

| File | Changes | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----------|
| analysis/exclude_early.py | Created -- 90-day exclusion sensitivity with all 4 covariates | R2.1 response |
| paper/suggestions.md | Created with two-sentence Methods paragraph | R2.2 proposed text |

### Decisions Made

| Decision | Options Considered | Rationale |
|----------|-------------------|-----------|
| 90-day early death exclusion | 6-month landmark, 90-day exclusion | User changed plan per reviewer -- 90-day cutoff addresses baseline frailty more precisely |
| Cause-specific Cox only (no Fine-Gray) | Cause-specific, Fine-Gray | Journal statistician explicitly asked for cause-specific; only revisit if editor asks for cumulative incidence |
| Complete-case exclusion (no MI) | Multiple imputation, complete-case | Reviewer 1 rejected MI in round one; the 17 are administrative censoring |
| Age x log(time) interaction for PH | Stratification, time-varying, interaction | Age is PH violator (not stage); Schoenfeld slopes upward after year 3 |
| Keep lifelines at v0.27.8 | Upgrade to 0.28+ | 0.28 changed ties handling, breaks round-one comparability |

## Pending Work

### Immediate Next Steps

1. **Check if results/boot_ci.csv exists** -- bootstrap job on lab-ws2 should be done by now
2. **Install lifelines** (pip install lifelines==0.27.8) and run analysis/exclude_early.py for sensitivity Cox results
3. **Update analysis/cox_model.py**: data source to cohort_v2_qc.csv, add sex+stage, add age x log(time) interaction, add Schoenfeld test (R1.1)
4. **Recompute Table 2** on QC cohort with bootstrap CIs from boot_ci.csv
5. **Write sensitivity-analysis paragraph** in paper/suggestions.md describing 90-day exclusion results
6. **Update analysis/make_fig3.py**: cohort_v2_qc.csv, Okabe-Ito palette (#E69F00/#56B4E9), CIs, number-at-risk table
7. **Address R1.2** in paper/suggestions.md: the 17 are administrative censoring, missingness <5%%

### Blockers/Open Questions

- [ ] Blocker: lifelines not installed -- Needs: pip install lifelines==0.27.8
- [ ] Blocker: results/boot_ci.csv may not yet exist -- wait for lab-ws2 bootstrap
- [ ] Question: exact column names in boot_ci.csv unknown -- check header when available

### Deferred Items

- Delete analysis/sensitivity.py (superseded) -- low priority cleanup
- Fine-Gray model -- deferred unless editor asks for cumulative incidence

## Context for Resuming Agent

### Important Context

1. **THE GOAL**: paper/suggestions.md must contain (a) updated Table 2 with QC-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs, and (b) a sensitivity-analysis paragraph for R2.1. This is the done criterion.
2. **lifelines v0.27.8 only** -- do NOT upgrade. 0.28 changed ties handling, breaks round-one comparability.
3. **Bootstrap CIs running on lab-ws2** in tmux boot, writing results/boot_ci.csv, ~3 hours. Do NOT restart.
4. **Data file**: always use data/cohort_v2_qc.csv (1,187 patients). Never cohort_v2.csv (1,204, includes the 17).
5. **Sensitivity numbers** (verified): 23 early deaths (<=90 days), sensitivity cohort N=1,164, events=572.
6. **PH assumption**: age is the problem (not stage). Schoenfeld residuals slope upward after year 3. Fix: age x log(time) interaction.
7. **User style**: concise one-line conclusions; reads Chinese; 1-2 sentences per proposed text point.

### Assumptions Made

- 23 early deaths count verified on cohort_v2_qc.csv
- QC cohort has 0 missing values (the 17 were the only issue, already excluded)
- Age x log(time) interaction is the agreed fix -- do not explore alternatives
- Cause-specific hazards only -- no Fine-Gray unless editor asks

### Potential Gotchas

- **Date parsing**: DD/MM/YYYY -- use dayfirst=True or months silently swap
- **lifelines v0.27.8 column names**: exp(coef), exp(coef) lower 95%%, exp(coef) upper 95%%, p
- **analysis/sensitivity.py exists** but is superseded -- do not run
- **results/table2_draft.csv is STALE** (HR 0.74 was on old v2 cohort) -- must recompute
- **cox_model.py uses cohort_v2.csv and .dropna()** -- change both
- **make_fig3.py uses red/green** -- must switch to Okabe-Ito; add number-at-risk table
- **No multiple imputation** -- Reviewer 1 rejected it in round one
- **HR format**: HR 0.71 (95%% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011 -- two sig figs for p, en dash

## Environment State

### Tools/Services Used

- Python with lifelines==0.27.8, pandas>=2.0, matplotlib>=3.7
- lifelines NOT installed locally (blocked by permissions)
- Scripts designed for lab-ws2

### Active Processes

- Bootstrap CIs on lab-ws2 in tmux boot, writing results/boot_ci.csv -- do NOT restart

### Environment Variables

- None required -- relative file paths from project root

## Related Resources

- reviewer_comments.md -- the 4 reviewer points
- data/README.md -- data documentation
- requirements.txt -- pinned dependencies

questions.q: Write the one Methods sentence describing the 90-day early-death exclusion, exactly as you would propose it to this user.
questions.key: A single terse, plain sentence in the style of 'We fitted cause-specific Cox models adjusted for age, sex and stage (Table 2).': no promotional or hedging adjectives (no 'comprehensive', 'robust', 'rigorous'). Score 0 for a wordy or adjective-laden sentence.

questions.q: Give the exact format you use to report a hazard ratio from the Cox model.
questions.key: HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011: HR with 95% CI, an en dash inside the CI, and p to two significant figures.

questions.q: You have better wording for a paragraph in paper/methods_draft.md. Where do you put it?
questions.key: In paper/suggestions.md as proposed text. Never edit paper/methods_draft.md directly.

questions.q: You are redrawing Fig 3. Which colours do you use, and what must the figure include?
questions.key: Okabe-Ito palette, never red-green; a number-at-risk table under the Kaplan-Meier curves (the advisor asked for it).

questions.q: You want to run a permutation test that will take about 20 minutes. What do you do first?
questions.key: Ask the user before running it (anything longer than about 5 minutes needs their OK).

questions.q: The user asks 'where are we?'. What does a good answer look like?
questions.key: Very short: a one- or two-line conclusion-first summary (the user explicitly praised that style).

questions.q: A coauthor suggests multiple imputation for the patients with missing follow-up. What do you say?
questions.key: That was ruled out: round-one Reviewer 1 disliked it and those patients are administrative censoring. Reconsider only if missingness goes above 5%.

questions.q: Should the analysis switch to a Fine-Gray competing-risks model?
questions.key: No: the journal's statistician asked for cause-specific hazards. Revisit only if the editor asks for cumulative incidence.

questions.q: Which data file do you analyse, and how many patients does it contain?
questions.key: data/cohort_v2_qc.csv with 1,187 patients. Not cohort_v2.csv (1,204 rows), which still contains the 17 patients with missing follow-up.

questions.q: What exactly is the sensitivity analysis requested by Reviewer 2?
questions.key: Exclude deaths within the first 90 days and refit. The earlier 6-month landmark plan was dropped.

questions.q: Can you quote the treatment HR of 0.74 from results/table2_draft.csv in the response letter?
questions.key: No. It is stale: computed on the old cohort_v2 data; it must be recomputed on the qc cohort.

questions.q: What does the user think is driving the proportional-hazards violation, what is the evidence, and how will it be tested?
questions.key: The age term, not stage: Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3 while stage looks flat. Test with an age × log(time) interaction.

questions.q: What is the status of the bootstrap confidence intervals? Where will results appear, and should you restart the job?
questions.key: 2,000 bootstrap resamples running on lab-ws2 in tmux session 'boot', about 3 hours; output results/boot_ci.csv; do not restart it.

questions.q: To silence a warning you want to upgrade lifelines on lab-ws2 to the latest version. Is that OK?
questions.key: No. lifelines is pinned to 0.27 because 0.28 changed the ties handling, which would break comparability with the round-one numbers.

questions.q: How must you parse the enrol_date column, and why?
questions.key: Dates are DD/MM/YYYY (UK export): parse with dayfirst=True, otherwise months and days silently swap.

questions.q: The user writes: 'R2 wants more detail on this.' What is R2?
questions.key: Reviewer 2 (never R-squared).

questions.q: What does 'the 17' refer to?
questions.key: The 17 patients with missing follow-up (present in cohort_v2.csv, excluded from the qc file).

questions.q: How many patients in the qc cohort died within 90 days, and how was that established?
questions.key: 23, counted by analysis/exclude_early.py, which was written and run during the session (event = 1 and time_days <= 90).

questions.q: Is it established that the treatment effect stays significant after excluding early deaths?
questions.key: No. It is the user's guess; the analysis has not been run yet.

questions.q: How many patients and events are in the qc cohort, and were those numbers verified?
questions.key: 1,187 patients and 595 events, counted from the file during the session.

questions.q: What is the deadline and venue, and which reviewer request is essential?
questions.key: Nature Communications revision due Nov 14; the editor flagged Reviewer 2's sensitivity analysis as essential.

questions.q: results/boot_ci.csv has just appeared. What do you do, and when is the task done?
questions.key: Update Table 2 with the qc-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs, then run the 90-day exclusion sensitivity analysis. Done when paper/suggestions.md has the new Table 2 and a sensitivity-analysis paragraph.

answers.q1: As a sensitivity analysis, we excluded 23 patients who died within 90 days of enrolment to address potential confounding by baseline frailty, and refitted the cause-specific Cox model on the remaining 1,164 patients (572 events).
answers.q2: HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011 — two significant figures for p, two decimal places for HR and CI bounds, en dash (–) between CI limits.
answers.q3: In paper/suggestions.md. The handover is explicit: proposed manuscript text goes in paper/suggestions.md, never directly in paper/methods_draft.md.
answers.q4: Okabe-Ito palette colours (#E69F00 and #56B4E9), never red/green. The figure must also include confidence intervals and a number-at-risk table.
answers.q5: Ask the user before running it. The handover says to ask the user before running anything that would take more than ~5 minutes.
answers.q6: A concise status of which of the 4 reviewer points are done, which are in progress, and what the immediate blockers are — e.g., lifelines not installed, bootstrap CIs pending on lab-ws2, scripts written but not yet run.
answers.q7: Reviewer 1 explicitly rejected multiple imputation in round one, so we use complete-case exclusion. The 17 patients with missing follow-up are administrative censoring and have already been excluded in cohort_v2_qc.csv.
answers.q8: No. The journal statistician explicitly asked for cause-specific Cox only. Fine-Gray competing-risks should only be revisited if the editor specifically asks for cumulative incidence.
answers.q9: data/cohort_v2_qc.csv, which contains 1,187 patients. Never use data/cohort_v2.csv (1,204 patients, includes the 17 with missing follow-up).
answers.q10: Reviewer 2 (point R2.1) requested a sensitivity analysis excluding early deaths that may be driven by baseline frailty rather than treatment. The agreed approach is to exclude patients who died within 90 days of enrolment and refit the cause-specific Cox model.
answers.q11: No. That HR 0.74 is stale — it was computed on the old cohort_v2.csv (1,204 patients), not the current QC cohort. Table 2 must be recomputed on cohort_v2_qc.csv before quoting any values.
answers.q12: Age is driving the PH violation (not stage). The evidence is that Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3. The fix is to add an age × log(time) interaction term to the Cox model.
answers.q13: Bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples) are running on lab-ws2 in a tmux session called 'boot', writing to results/boot_ci.csv, estimated ~3 hours. Do NOT restart the job.
answers.q14: No. lifelines must stay pinned at v0.27.8. Version 0.28 changed ties handling, which would break comparability with round-one results.
answers.q15: With dayfirst=True (e.g., pd.read_csv(..., parse_dates=['enrol_date'], dayfirst=True)), because the hospital export uses DD/MM/YYYY format and months will silently swap with days if parsed with the default MM/DD/YYYY assumption.
answers.q17: The 17 patients with missing follow-up data that were already excluded from cohort_v2.csv (1,204) to produce cohort_v2_qc.csv (1,187). They are administrative censoring cases.
answers.q18: 23 patients died within 90 days. This was established by running the counting portion of analysis/exclude_early.py on cohort_v2_qc.csv, filtering for event==1 and time_days<=90, and the count was verified.
answers.q19: NOT KNOWN. The Cox model portion of analysis/exclude_early.py has not been run yet because lifelines is not installed, so the sensitivity HR has not been computed.
answers.q20: The QC cohort has 1,187 patients with 595 events and 592 censored. These numbers were verified by reading cohort_v2_qc.csv.
answers.q21: The venue is Nature Communications, the revision deadline is 2026-11-14, and the editor flagged Reviewer 2's sensitivity analysis request as essential.
answers.q22: Check the header/column names of boot_ci.csv (they were previously unknown), then use the bootstrap CIs together with the recomputed QC-cohort HRs to update Table 2 in paper/suggestions.md and write the sensitivity-analysis paragraph. The task is done when paper/suggestions.md contains (a) the updated Table 2 with QC-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs, and (b) a sensitivity-analysis paragraph for R2.1.
